territorial_scope.description: Applies to providers designated by name by the Fair Trade Commission; the secrecy-order offence also applies to acts committed outside Japan.

evidence.quote: 日本国外において同項の罪を犯した者にも適用する

summary.short: Japan's Act on Promotion of Competition for Specified Smartphone Software designates providers of smartphone basic software, app stores, browsers and search engines above size thresholds. It bars them from favouring their own offerings, misusing third-party data and unfairly treating app providers, and requires disclosure, data transfer and default-setting measures.
summary.long: The Act sets rules for designated providers of four categories of smartphone software: basic software, app stores, browsers and search engines. The Fair Trade Commission designates providers whose business scale meets a size set by cabinet order, using indicators such as user numbers, and designated providers must notify the Commission of their scale. Designated providers may not use data obtained from third-party app or website operators to compete with them, may not impose unfair terms on app providers, may not restrict alternative app stores, payment systems, browser engines or the display of offers made through external web pages, and may not favour their own services in search results. They must disclose conditions for acquiring data, allow users to have their data transferred, implement default-setting and choice-screen measures, and file annual reports. The Commission may issue recommendations and exclusion orders. Surcharges of 20% of relevant sales apply to breaches of Articles 7 and 8, rising to 30% for repeat cases. Damages liability applies without a defence of absence of fault, and criminal penalties apply to breaches of secrecy orders and final exclusion orders. The Act takes effect on a date set by cabinet order no later than 18 months after promulgation, with some provisions effective on promulgation and others six months later.

enforcement.authority: 公正取引委員会 (Fair Trade Commission)
enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of Arts 5 to 9 (prohibited conduct of designated providers)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No monetary maximum. Order to cease the conduct and take measures to eliminate the violation, including partial business transfer
enforcement.penalty_formula: Not applicable. Art. 18 para. 2 allows corrective measures (e.g., notice that the conduct has ended) even after the conduct has ceased, but not more than 3 years after it ceased
enforcement.cure_period: No cure period stated. Commitment procedure under Arts 22 to 24 is separate

evidence.quote: 公正取引委員会は、指定事業者に対し、当該行為の差止め、事業の一部の譲渡その他これらの規定に違反する行為を排除するために必要な措置を命ずることができる。

enforcement.authority: 公正取引委員会 (Fair Trade Commission)
enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of Art. 7 or Art. 8 (items 1 and 2 only), i.e., prohibited conduct regarding basic software or app stores
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Surcharge (課徴金) of 20% of sales of the violating goods or services during the violation period; 30% in the cases listed in Art. 20
enforcement.penalty_formula: 20% x sales amount of the relevant goods or services during the violation period (Art. 19 para. 1); 30% instead of 20% under Art. 20 for specified repeat or successor cases; sales may be estimated under Art. 19 para. 2 if the firm refuses to report or provide facts; amounts below JPY 10,000 are truncated (Art. 21 para. 2); no order may be made 3 years after the violation period ends (Art. 21 para. 5)
enforcement.cure_period: No cure period stated. A remediation plan (排除措置計画) may be submitted within 60 days of notice (Art. 23 para. 1); if certified, Art. 18 and Art. 19 para. 1 do not apply to the covered conduct (Art. 24)

evidence.quote: 当該違反行為に係る商品又は役務の売上額に、百分の二十を乗じて得た額に相当する額の課徴金を国庫に納付することを命じなければならない。
